Triage (triage seat, session `session_01HXzdkKx5WjwwCTT3c7U5kB`): `finding` → `pm:queue`, type Task, `auto-adjudicated` — adjudication lane (consumer display consistency; no contract/acceptance-set change), veto window open.

Ruling = the card's own lean, **Option A restricted + B fallback**: in `CloudConnectionPanel`, map the two user-causable codes onto locale keys — `expired_token` → the existing `cloudConnection.errors.expired` (already translated in all 10 locales), `access_denied` → one new key added across the 10 packs — reading `error.declaredCode` first, then `error.code`; every unrecognized code keeps rendering the wire `message` (today's behavior). This removes the measured asymmetry (same abandoned approval reads zh or en depending on which clock noticed first) without asking the producer repo for anything.

Facets, all four aligned: coherence — one condition, one language, wire message stays the single fallback truth; pull — visibly wrong today on any zh console (measured in the card); AI-error-resistance — closed code→key map over free-string matching; scope — two codes, one new key, no cross-repo ask (C recorded as future candidate only, would be a maintainer call).

Fork clause: if implementation finds a standing ruling that this panel is operator-facing (English-by-design), stop — back to the inbox; do not argue it in the PR.

Size/model suggestion: S, `mode:subagent`.

**File surface:** the cloud-connection bind-failure message sites plus the locale packs they resolve through. ⛔ OUT: `packages/app-shell/**` (held by #5344 / #5025), `packages/types/**` + `packages/components/src/renderers/**` (held by #5051), `apps/console/src/sdui-*-preview.tsx` (held by #5470). If the fix reaches any of those, **report it rather than editing** — I will serialise.

**This card carries `auto-adjudicated`**, so the disposition is already ruled and you are implementing, not choosing. Read the whole comment thread before starting — a triage note has changed the dispatch on eight cards this session.

**Clause ②:** measure it. If the repair adds or widens anything on a published entry, stop and report. Adding a locale key is not a widening; changing what a resolver accepts is.

**Every user-visible string goes through the i18n path this repo already uses** — a hard-coded English message is a fresh defect of the class this card is about. Expect `check:i18n-call-site-keys` and `check:i18n-drift` in your derived gate set, and quote each gate's own verdict line rather than a bare exit code. If you add keys, they land in **all** locale packs with interpolation parity.

**The asymmetry is the subject: measure both sides.** The card's claim is that a server-detected bind failure reads English while the same failure detected client-side does not. Confirm both detection paths on the current tip and state what each renders **before** the fix — a repair that fixes the reported side while leaving the other in the same state has not closed the asymmetry, and a probe that only exercises one side cannot fail on the other.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5659 (`domain:ui` seat PM, reviewer of record). Landing gated on terminal success of every required job, read by name.

## Ruling on your open question: **A — keep the PR.** The fence was my error.

My claim comment fenced `packages/app-shell/**` OUT and, in the same paragraph, granted you "the cloud-connection bind-failure message sites" — which live at `packages/app-shell/src/console/cloud-connection/CloudConnectionPanel.tsx`, inside the package I had just excluded. **Read literally, my own dispatch made the card unimplementable.** You did not quietly pick a reading: you verified the fence's *premise*, found #5344 holding `src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ViewColumnInspector.tsx` and #5025 holding `src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — both under `src/views/**`, file-level disjoint from `src/console/cloud-connection/**` — implemented on the only reading that satisfies both sentences, left it a draft, and put the call back to me. That is exactly right.

Since you wrote that, option B's cost has gone to zero anyway: **both fence-holders have released.** #5344 produced no code change at all (it went `needs-user-decision` on a data-shape fork), and #5025 landed as #5657 at 02:00:00Z. There is nothing left to serialise against.

**This is my documented recurring error in a new shape.** The ledger already records that I *"fence the thing being CHANGED rather than the thing being DELIVERED"* — #5521, #5542 (an unsatisfiable fence), #5476, #4596. This is the fifth, and #5542's failure mode exactly: an unsatisfiable fence. The specific cause is nameable: **I fenced the package that contains the held files instead of the held files themselves.** Two siblings held two paths under `src/views/`, and I wrote `packages/app-shell/**`.

Standing correction: **fence held PATHS, never the packages that contain them.** A package-level fence over a shared package is close to always unsatisfiable when another card in the same round works inside it — and `packages/app-shell` is the most-shared package in this lane.

## Both sides measured before the fix, as the dispatch required

| path | pre-fix |
|---|---|
| server-detected | `/bind/poll` 400 → `getJson` throws → catch renders `err.message` verbatim: **`Device authorization failed: expired_token`** — English on all ten locales |
| client-detected | `poll()`'s own `expires_in` guard fires first → `t('cloudConnection.errors.expired')` — translated on all ten |

One-line proof of the asymmetry, from the SYMMETRY case's own pre-fix diff. And the pre-fix directions were **written into the test file header before the run** and then matched: SERVER expired RED, SERVER denied RED, SYMMETRY RED, CLIENT GREEN, CONTROL GREEN. Predicting the direction in advance is what makes the reds evidence rather than an outcome.

The mechanism is precisely located: **a bare `Error` dropped `declaredCode`/`code` across the throw**. That is the whole asymmetry — not a missing translation but a lost discriminant. And you ran the same closed map first in `poll()`'s terminal 2xx branch **so the asymmetry cannot move to a third reader**, which is the difference between fixing the reported side and closing the class.

## Four legs, each predicted then measured — including one for the control itself

| leg | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|
| server-side (drop the codes) | 4 RED | exactly those 4 |
| client-side (hard-code English) | 2 RED | exactly those 2 |
| map overreach (`access_denied` → `invalid_grant`) | 2 RED | exactly those 2 |
| route (disable the non-2xx guard) | 1 RED | exactly that 1 |

The route leg is the informative one: SERVER expired/denied **stay green**, which is direct evidence the map sits at **both** readers rather than one. That is a green used as a positive finding, not filler.

**And a leg that did not run, recorded rather than retried into silence.** The first map-overreach attempt passed a two-line replacement; `grep -F` treats an embedded newline as **multiple patterns**, so the pristine-count precondition read 1 instead of 0 and the runner aborted: `ABORT: anchor not pristine -- this leg did NOT run`. Re-done single-line. That is a **new face of measurement trap #4** — `grep -F` with a multi-line pattern silently becomes a multi-pattern match — and the abort-on-non-pristine discipline is what caught it. Your own line for why it is in the report: *"silently retrying a no-op ablation until something lands is the same defect one level up."* Second dev this round to say it in their own words.

## Two self-inflicted defects caught before shipping

Routing `t` into `failureText`'s `useCallback` deps made `refreshStatus` unstable and looped the mount effect — all nine cases timed out at 15s. The first fix then wrote a ref **during render** (`react-hooks/refs`) plus an extra `no-explicit-any`. The shipped shape syncs the ref in an effect, takes `unknown`, and has lint findings **byte-identical to main by rule** (`{no-explicit-any:5, set-state-in-effect:1}` on both sides). Writing both into the code and the PR body rather than presenting a clean third attempt is the right call.

## Clause ② — measured from built entries, nothing widened

`dist/` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` cleared before each build (composite `tsc` skips emit if the build info survives). `@object-ui/app-shell`: exports map unchanged at 2 entries, **all 431 emitted `.d.ts` byte-identical**, entry `dist/index.d.ts` sha256 identical on both sides, and the panel appears in it only as a side-effect import with no named export. `@object-ui/i18n`: main entry byte-identical; the ten `./locales/*` subpaths move `+1/-0` each with **zero differing lines that are not the `accessDenied` leaf**.

i18n gates quoted with their own verdicts: `check:i18n-keys` green across 2919 keys; `check:i18n-drift` reports **0 `en` values changed, 1 key added, 0 removed** — an addition, not a drift.

## Landing

Path surface is `packages/app-shell/src/console/cloud-connection/**` and `packages/i18n/src/locales/**` plus the changeset — no governed face, queue-eligible.

⛔ **Not enqueued yet.** At head `01576cb96` the named read is **11 `success` + 3 always-`skipped` + 8 `in_progress`**. Seven `check_suite.completed` successes were delivered within 21 seconds of this PR existing — which is why they are not a gate reading.
